messages:
mika: Heads-up — after the selective-kernel-change merged in the 22:30 deploy we've seen a cluster of longctx OOMs on prod-gpu-pools. First noticed ~22:45 in canary.
Alex: saw that too, repro on a 64k seqlen job. Memory jumps during kv-attach step.
Priya: is this the kernel selection fallback change? I remember that PR touched kernel routing and batching heuristic timing.
mika: yeah, PR #4578 — it added a 'prefer-fast-kernel' cost that biases smaller batches to a different kernel path. Might be interacting with our slab allocator.
Carlos: can you paste the error? logs looked like vmem alloc failed then oom-killer.
mika: logs:
```
2026-03-17T22:46:12Z runtime ERROR: KVCache::attach failed: out_of_memory (requested=348MB, avail=120MB)
stack: runtime::attach_kv +0x1a3, kernel_select::dispatch +0x7f
```
jamie: interestingly, regression appears only when sequence lengths > 32k and when batching peaks. Shorter seqs fine.
Li: I ran a quick flamegraph on canary. KV compaction dominates now — compaction frequency increased ~3x after the deploy.
Priya: that smells like fragmentation. If kernel selection changes access patterns (chunk sizes) we could be getting more slab splits.
Alex: I bisected locally. Reverting commit a1b2c3 (kernel routing tweak) reduces OOMs on our repro to zero. With the commit, memory highwater mark +25%.
mika: can we roll back the release? It's blocking all long-context customers.
deploy-bot: @channel deploy reverted: revert-4578 was applied to prod at 23:05 UTC by jamie. Rollback ID: r-20260317-4578
ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-0317 created for longctx OOM regression; severity P1, assigned to eng-runtime.
Carlos: re-run of failed jobs after revert shows drop in fragmentation metrics. But we should still root-cause upstream; revert is emergency mitigation.
Priya: timeline for analysis: I'll gather allocator metrics and a heapshot diff. Mika — can you capture KV slab histograms and the kernel selection logs for the window 22:30-23:05?
mika: grabbing them now. commands used:
```
# capture slab hist
curl -sS http://canary-metrics/local/kv/slab_hist | jq . > /tmp/slab_hist.json
# kernel select trace
kubectl logs runtime-canary -c router --since=40m | grep kernel_select > /tmp/kernel_select.log
```
Alex: on my repro box I dumped kv entries and saw a lot of tiny fragments due to chunk split logic in compaction. Suspect path in kernel X changes stride to 256 vs prior 512 which increases split rate.
Li: attaching quick profile snapshot (summarized):
- pre-change: compaction CPU 6% of run
- post-change: compaction CPU 22% of run, mem alloc churn high
jamie: PR #4590 (compaction heuristic) landed earlier in the week; could be second-order effect. We need to check merge windows overlap.
Carlos: I started a git-merge-bisect between 4578 and 4590. Early signal points to 4578 as primary but combined with 4590 amplifies frag.
Priya: action items:
- confirm: revert remains in prod (jamie) :white_check_mark:
- run targeted fuzz with seqlen distribution skewed to long tails (mika + Alex)
- add sampler to log kernel selection + batch size per request (Li)
- evaluate kernel X stride change and revert if necessary (Carlos)
- add CI perf test for fragmentation regression (jamie)
mika: repro command for fuzz:
```
python tools/fuzz_longctx.py --seq-dist 'powerlaw' --max-seq 65536 --rps 5 --duration 30m --target canary
```
Alex: I'll try toggling kernel preference flags locally: `--prefer-fast-kernel=false` and `--kv-compact-threshold=0.2` to reproduce behavior matrix.
Li: also tagging memory profiler on the canary runtime to capture allocation stack traces: `--alloc-trace=on` for the next run.
jamie: once we have minimal reproducer and allocator traces let's open a proper perf issue and assign to kernel/runtime owners. Also add a rollback-tolerant test in pre-merge CI that simulates long tails.
mika: one more note — customers hit were mostly on Dedicated pools with larger batch windows; hosted small bursts didn't show it. routing policy difference may have exposed it.
Carlos: agreed. Might need policy-level safeguard to prefer smaller batches when long-seq flags present.
Priya: ok I'll own the forensic ticket. Moving to postmortem after root cause. Thanks all for rapid rollback and triage :raised_hands:
ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-0317 status: mitigated (revert applied). Next update scheduled in 4h or on new findings.
Alex: leaving logs and traces in /tmp/kv-frag-1898745123.tar.gz on canary-host; ping me if you need access.
mika: wrapping up — will run fuzzer overnight and dump results in the incident thread. :eyes:
